headline: Quantum Control, Code Structure, and Noise Limits
summary: Today's selection bridges fundamental quantum information limits with physical implementation challenges. Key theoretical results pin down optimal unitary estimation and decouple topological CSS codes and fracton orders. Concurrently, new protocols address realistic open-system physics via non-Gaussian noise characterization and robust gate drives.

themes.title: Topological Phases and Quantum Code Decoupling
themes.body: Algebraic frameworks advance our understanding of topological matter, showing how higher-dimensional CSS codes decouple into toric codes and formalizing fracton excitations via braided fusion complexes.

themes.title: Optimal Gate Bounds and Coherent Control
themes.body: Analytical Hamiltonian engineering suppresses infidelity in strongly driven single qubits, while query complexity analysis bounds the ultimate speed of unitary diamond distance estimation.

themes.title: Open Systems and Non-Classical Statistics
themes.body: Novel probes capture delicate open-system dynamics, utilizing exceptional points to witness non-Gaussian dephasing and multi-detector interferometry to track spin-dependent photon fluctuations.

connections.body: Both papers address translation-invariant, spatially structured topological orders by classifying mobile versus immobile excitations and characterizing their non-trivial algebraic entanglements.
